report:
Reviewed the complete typed_interning claim and all 2 ordinary implementation associations and 11 ordinary associated tests. No TODO or N/A evidence is present. Requirements are stash-local content addressing for every scalar and slice allocation, reuse of a handle for equal typed structural content, and content comparison to distinguish hash collisions. In sage-stash/src/lib.rs each Stash owns its own intern_map. alloc keys candidates by StaticSelf TypeId, count=1, content hash and collision ordinal, compares the stored T using PartialEq before returning its entry index, and stores unequal colliders at subsequent ordinals. alloc_slice hashes length and elements, includes element count in the same key, compares entire typed slices, and follows the same collision search; alloc_slice_from_iter collects and delegates. append_one and deep copies likewise delegate to allocation. TypeId uniqueness is an explicit StashData safety obligation. push_raw, typed readers and handle construction preserve the selected entry. Including count prevents an empty-slice/scalar hash collision from reading nonexistent scalar data. InternHasher uses child entries' hashes; within a stash canonical child indices make derived PartialEq comparisons structural for nested Ptr and Slice fields. The macro association generates fieldwise hashing for named and tuple fields and discriminant plus field hashing for enum variants; unit fields produce an empty stream. No essential local implementation dependency lies outside the two associated whole files.
Test adequacy: alloc_same_value_deduplicates and hash_cons_distinct assert equal and unequal scalar handles; hash_cons_slice_dedup and hash_cons_slice_distinct do the same for slices. hash_cons_compound_type exercises a derived pair of child handles. dedup_different_types_same_bits checks typed retrieval of distinct named types (its Name and Tag fields have different integer widths, so it is not alone proof of identical bit layouts); typed_scalars_slices_and_derived_nested_values_deduplicate additionally checks same-width signed/unsigned scalar retrieval, repeated scalars, iterator/slice allocation equivalence, derived nested Branch scalar and slice reuse, and empty iterator/slice reuse. hash_cons_collision_stores_both forces identical hashes for unequal scalars and ordered slices, asserts distinct handles and correct retrieval, and asserts reuse for equal colliders. derived_values_and_slices_resolve_forced_hash_collisions_by_content repeats those substantive assertions through the derive-generated field hashing path. Captured EmptySliceCollision hashes a constant and DerivedCollision wraps it, so these are actual forced collisions. scalar_collision_with_empty_slice_never_reads_a_slice_as_a_scalar forces an empty-slice hash collision in both insertion orders and asserts scalar retrieval, empty contents, and repeat reuse; empty_unit_slice_and_scalar_do_not_confuse_interning covers zero-sized scalar/empty-slice reuse. Assertions would detect both accidental collision sharing and failure to deduplicate. Fixtures Point, Name, Tag, Branch, EmptySliceCollision and DerivedCollision were captured via review read. The guarantee is scoped to one stash and uses the supplied types' structural hashing/equality contracts, not cross-stash handle identity.
Execution separate from inspection: ran cargo test -p sage-stash --test arena_tests --test storage_contracts successfully: 46 arena tests and 9 storage-contract tests passed, including all 11 associated tests. No source edits were made. The reviewed implementation and combined assertions account for the complete claim; no edits requested.
